newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU farm chief says Britain made mistakes over BSE.
newsitem.headline: EU farm chief says Britain made mistakes over BSE.

text.p: Serious errors have been made in Britain over the handling of mad cow disease, the European Union's Farm Commissioner said in remarks published on Tuesday.
"It is clear that serious mistakes have been committed in Great Britain," Franz Fischler said in an interview with the Paris daily Le Monde.
"These mistakes are not so much in the health measures that have been taken against this new disease, but in the way they have been carried out and checked," the Austrian official said.
The crisis over mad cow disease will cost the European Union 3.5 billion Ecus ($4.4 billion) by the end of 1997, he said.
Fischler's remarks came a day after Britain said it would slaughter 100,000 more cattle, in a U-turn aimed at persuading the EU to lift a nine-month-old ban on British beef exports.

Fischler on Monday ruled out a speedy end to the ban, imposed in March after London reported a suspected link between mad cow disease, or bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), and a fatal brain disorder in humans.
A selective cattle cull was agreed between Britain and its EU partners at a summit in June but London suspended the plan in September, saying fresh evidence suggested it was unnecessary.
European Union farm ministers were meeting in Brussels on Tuesday amid French calls for a review of aid to veal producers also hit by the slump of consumer confidence in beef.
Fischler said his estimate of the cost of tackling the crisis included slaughtering programmes, compensation to herdsmen and EU-controlled beef purchases to prop up prices.
